# 4 Calibration and quantification

```{r}
#| label: calib-data
CAL_MAT <- util$mat_id_in_calibration(BLK)
gcal <- tr[["global calibration"]][[BLK]]
multi_batch <- length(batch_ids) > 1 && !is.null(gcal)
in_log <- isTRUE(tr$params$log_calibration)
name2id <- setNames(smp$sample_id, smp$sample_name)
# Averaged calibration points (option): ID = name
if (!is.null(cal_avg) && nrow(cal_avg) > 0) name2id <- c(name2id, setNames(cal_avg$sample_id, cal_avg$sample_name))

curve_grid <- function(lloq, uloq) {
  if (in_log) exp(seq(log(lloq), log(uloq), length.out = 120)) else
    sort(unique(c(seq(lloq, uloq, length.out = 100), seq(lloq, min(lloq * 10, uloq), length.out = 40))))
}
# Curve from the coefficients of the fit of signal on concentration
curve_from_coef <- function(cf, lloq, uloq) {
  if (is.null(cf) || !is.finite(lloq) || !is.finite(uloq)) return(NULL)
  x <- curve_grid(lloq, uloq); xx <- if (in_log) log(x) else x
  y <- cf[1] + cf[2] * xx + if (length(cf) > 2) cf[3] * xx^2 else 0
  if (in_log) y <- expm1(y)
  npts(x = sig(x), y = sig(y))
}
# Point lists stay JSON arrays also with a single point (`to_json` unboxes length-1 vectors)
npts <- function(...) lapply(list(...), I)
model_label <- function(nm) if (is.null(nm) || is.na(nm)) NULL else sub("_div_", "/", nm)

global_view <- function(fid) {
  i <- match(fid, gcal$limits$feature_id)
  if (is.na(i)) return(NULL)
  L <- gcal$limits[i, ]
  okc <- !is.na(gcal$cal_signal[fid, ]) & !is.na(gcal$cal_conc)
  xs <- gcal$conc0[fid, ]; ys <- gcal$signal[fid, ]; oks <- !is.na(xs) & !is.na(ys)
  list(src = if (isTRUE(L$has_proper_range)) "Global" else "None",
       notes = util$calib_notes(L, batch_view = FALSE),   # For table 4.2 (not in the viewer data)
       why = show$calib_issue_text(L, batch_view = FALSE), kept = isTRUE(L$kept_calcurve),
       nq = show$calib_range_note(L),
       lod = sig(L$lod), lloq = sig(L$lloq), uloq = sig(L$uloq %||% L$max_c_conc), top = sig(L$max_c_conc),
       model = model_label(L$model), r2 = if (is.na(L$r2)) NULL else round(L$r2, 3),
       # Also a curve that is not valid (e.g. R² below the minimum), when it was fitted
       curve = curve_from_coef(L$coef[[1]], L$lloq, L$max_c_conc),
       cal = npts(x = sig(gcal$cal_conc[okc]), y = sig(gcal$cal_signal[fid, okc]),
                  u = as.integer(gcal$cal_used[fid, okc]), s = unname(s_idx[id2name[names(which(okc))]])),
       smp = npts(x = sig(xs[oks]), y = sig(ys[oks]), s = unname(s_idx[id2name[names(which(oks))]])))
}
batch_view <- function(x, fid) {
  if (!fid %in% rownames(x$concn)) return(NULL)
  rd <- SumExp::row_df(x$concn)[fid, ]
  cc <- x$calcurve[fid, ]; cs <- x$concn[fid, ]
  ccd <- SumExp::col_df(cc); csd <- SumExp::col_df(cs)
  ok_c <- !is.na(cc[[BLK]][1, ]) & !is.na(ccd$c_conc)
  xs <- cs[["conc0"]][1, ]; ys <- cs[[CAL_MAT]][1, ]; ok_s <- !is.na(xs) & !is.na(ys)
  m <- rd$calcurve_model[[1]]
  # Points used for the curve; for a batch using the global curve, those used by the global fit
  used <- !is.na(cc[[CAL_MAT]][1, ok_c])
  if (isTRUE(rd$src_calcurve == "Global") && !is.null(gcal)) {
    used <- gcal$cal_used[fid, name2id[ccd$sample_name[ok_c]]]
  }
  has_m <- is.list(m) && !is.null(m$best_model_name)
  list(src = if (is.na(rd$src_calcurve)) "None" else rd$src_calcurve,
       notes = util$calib_notes(rd),   # For table 4.2 (not in the viewer data)
       why = show$calib_issue_text(rd), kept = isTRUE(rd$kept_calcurve),
       nq = show$calib_range_note(rd),
       lod = sig(rd$lod), lloq = sig(rd$lloq), uloq = sig(rd$uloq %||% rd$max_c_conc), top = sig(rd$max_c_conc),
       model = if (has_m) model_label(m$best_model_name) else NULL,
       r2 = if (has_m) round(m$R2s[[m$best_model_name]], 3) else NULL,
       # Also a curve that is not valid (e.g. R² below the minimum), when it was fitted
       curve = if (has_m) curve_from_coef(unname(stats::coef(m$inv_model)), rd$lloq, rd$max_c_conc) else NULL,
       cal = npts(x = sig(ccd$c_conc[ok_c]), y = sig(cc[[BLK]][1, ok_c]), u = as.integer(used),
                  s = unname(s_idx[ccd$sample_name[ok_c]])),
       smp = npts(x = sig(xs[ok_s]), y = sig(ys[ok_s]), s = unname(s_idx[csd$sample_name[ok_s]])))
}
# Removed compounds have no calibration: show their calibration points (normalized signal)
cal_cols <- util$ctrl_smpl_cat(norm_all) == "CalCurve"
cal_conc <- util$spiked_conc_pts(norm_all)
removed_view <- function(fid, batch = NULL) {
  keep <- cal_cols
  if (!is.null(batch)) keep <- keep & as.character(SumExp::col_df(norm_all)$batch_id) == batch
  list(src = "None", cal = npts(x = sig(cal_conc[keep]), y = sig(norm_all[[MAT]][fid, keep]),
                                u = rep(0L, sum(keep)), s = unname(s_idx[SumExp::col_df(norm_all)$sample_name[keep]])))
}

# View name -> batch ID ("Global": the global curve of all batches)
view_ids <- c(if (multi_batch) c(Global = "Global"), setNames(batch_ids, batch_label(batch_ids)))
view_names <- names(view_ids)
tcomps <- feat |> filter(type == "Targeted") |> arrange(feature_name)
in_calib_ids <- rownames(lst[[1]]$concn)
cal_data <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tcomps)), function(k) {
  fid <- tcomps$feature_id[k]
  in_calib <- fid %in% in_calib_ids
  v <- lapply(view_names, function(nm) {
    if (!in_calib) return(removed_view(fid, if (nm == "Global") NULL else view_ids[[nm]]))
    if (nm == "Global") global_view(fid) else batch_view(lst[[view_ids[[nm]]]], fid)
  })
  names(v) <- view_names
  note <- if (!in_calib) {
    r <- removed_tgt$reason[match(fid, removed_tgt$feature_id)]
    paste("Removed before calibration:", if (is.na(r)) "no signal" else r)
  } else if (!any(vapply(v, \(x) !is.null(x) && x$src != "None", logical(1)))) {
    "No valid calibration range in any batch or globally"
  } else ""
  list(name = tcomps$feature_name[k], note = note, v = v)
})
```

`r if (AVERAGE_CAL) paste0('<div class="callout-q">The calibration replicates were averaged within each batch (one point per concentration level and batch, named "CalAvg_B&lt;batch&gt;_&lt;concentration&gt;"). ', if (length(batch_ids) > 1) 'Each batch is calibrated with its own averaged points (the global curve, on the averaged points of all batches, where a batch curve is not valid).' else 'The curve of all samples has one point per concentration level and batch.', ' The RSD% 20% threshold and the SD of the zero calibrant are not used.</div>') else ""`

## 4.1 Calibration curve samples

```{r}
# The same table as 2.2 (and the app's 2.2)
show$calib_samples_per_batch(raw, unit) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "l") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
```

## 4.2 Calibration curve limits {#calib-limits}

The LOD and LLOQ are the lowest calibration levels whose mean signal exceeds 3 and 10 times the blank
(Cal0) signal, the usual signal-to-noise criteria [@ichq2r2]; with the RSD% option, the replicates of
the LLOQ level must also have an RSD% of at most 20% [@ichm10]. The curves are linear or quadratic, with
the weighting 1, 1/x or 1/x² [@almeida2002].
`r uloq_txt <- if (in_log) "The ULOQ is the top of the linear range of the log–log curve found by SCALiR (slope 1; the points farthest from the line are left out until the mean squared residual is at most 0.01, with at least 3 points) [@ponce2024], but at least the minimum number of levels." else if (is.null(tr$params$linear_range_tol)) "The ULOQ is the highest calibration level of a linear curve; a quadratic curve has no ULOQ (empty)." else paste0("The ULOQ is the top of the linear range of a linear curve: while the back-calculated mean signal of the top level deviates more than ", tr$params$linear_range_tol, "% from its nominal concentration, that level is left out and the curve refitted, keeping at least ", tr$params$min_cal_points, " levels. A quadratic curve has no ULOQ (empty)."); paste(uloq_txt, if (is.null(tr$params$linear_range_tol)) "Concentrations above the ULOQ are extrapolated." else if (isTRUE(tr$params$enforce_linear_range)) "The curves were cut at the ULOQ and refitted (the levels above it are named in the notes); higher concentrations are extrapolated." else "The curves were not cut at the ULOQ: concentrations between the ULOQ and the top of the curve are above the linear range (\"> ULOQ, within curve\"), higher ones are extrapolated. The levels above the ULOQ are named in the notes.")`

One row per compound and curve. *IS* is the internal standard assigned to the compound (closest in
retention time), used by the Closest RT normalization. *Notes* shows an icon per kind of note (hover
it for the full note): why a curve is not valid (red rows), why a curve was kept although it is not
valid (orange rows; option "Keep all calibration curves"`r if (isTRUE(tr$params$keep_all_calcurves)) ", selected for this report" else ", not selected for this report"`),
why a batch uses the global curve, the levels above the ULOQ, and when no sample reaches the LLOQ.
The exported tables have the notes as text.

```{r}
is_of <- SumExp::row_df(lst[[1]]$concn) |> tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "feature_id") |>
  select(feature_id, IS = closest_istd)
lim_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(cal_data, function(cd) {
  purrr::map_dfr(names(cd$v), function(nm) {
    v <- cd$v[[nm]]
    if (is.null(v) || startsWith(cd$note, "Removed")) return(NULL)
    tibble(Compound = cd$name, Curve = nm, `Curve used` = v$src,
           Status = if (v$src == "None") "Not valid" else if (isTRUE(v$kept)) "Kept (not valid)" else
             if (nm != "Global" && v$src == "Global") "Global curve used" else "Valid",
           LOD = v$lod %||% NA, LLOQ = v$lloq %||% NA, ULOQ = v$uloq %||% NA,
           Model = v$model %||% NA, `R²` = v$r2 %||% NA,
           Notes = show$calib_notes_html(v$notes))
  })
}) |>
  left_join(transmute(tcomps, Compound = feature_name, feature_id), by = "Compound") |>
  left_join(is_of, by = "feature_id") |> select(-feature_id) |>
  mutate(Curve = factor(Curve, levels = view_names), `Curve used` = factor(`Curve used`),
         Status = factor(Status))
# Red: no valid calibration curve for the compound (in that curve); orange: kept although not valid
dt(lim_tbl, escape = setdiff(names(lim_tbl), "Notes"),   # The note icons are HTML
   caption = htmltools::HTML(show$calib_notes_legend_html(setdiff(names(util$calib_note_categories), "removed")))) |>
  DT::formatRound("R²", digits = 3) |>   # Always 3 decimals (also 0.950)
  DT::formatStyle("Status", target = "row",
                  backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c("Not valid", "Kept (not valid)"), c(FAILED_BG, KEPT_BG)))
```

### 4.2.1 Calibration models

```{r}
r2_long <- purrr::map_dfr(batch_ids, function(b) {
  rd <- SumExp::row_df(lst[[b]]$concn)
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(rd)), function(i) {
    m <- rd$calcurve_model[[i]]
    if (!is.list(m) || is.null(m$R2s_adj) || !isTRUE(rd$has_proper_range[i]) || !identical(rd$src_calcurve[i], "Batch")) return(NULL)
    tibble(batch = batch_label(b), model = sub("_div_", "/", names(m$R2s_adj)), r2 = m$R2s_adj,
           best = names(m$R2s_adj) == m$best_model_name)
  })
})
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Adjusted R² per model type

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.5
if (nrow(r2_long) == 0) note("No batch-wise calibration curves (all batches use the global curve).") else
ggplot(r2_long, aes(model, r2, fill = batch)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(max(0, quantile(r2_long$r2, .02, na.rm = TRUE)), 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Adjusted R² (quadratic penalized)", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

#### Chosen model

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4
best <- if (nrow(r2_long) == 0) tibble(curve = character(), model = character(), n = integer()) else
  r2_long |> filter(best) |> count(curve = batch, model)
if (multi_batch) best <- bind_rows(best, gcal$limits |> filter(has_proper_range) |>
                                     count(model = sub("_div_", "/", model)) |> mutate(curve = "Global"))
ggplot(best, aes(n, model, fill = curve)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Number of compounds", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

## 4.4 Calibration curves per chemical

The calibration curve of each targeted compound, also those without a valid calibration or removed
by a filter, as in the app (4.4), in two modes: **Calibration inspection** shows all calibration
points coloured by their role (within the calibration range, above the ULOQ, at the LOD, Cal0, out of
range), one symbol per batch; **Final calibration model** shows the fitted curve, the calibration
points it was fitted on, and the QCs (blue; the QC group in the hover text) and study samples (by
class) at their concentration, values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules as open circles. Grey areas are
below the LOD and the LLOQ, the olive area above the ULOQ; the parameters of the curve are shown
above the plot. `r if (multi_batch) "Choose the curve: **Global** (all batches) or a batch, which shows the curve used for that batch (its own, or the global one if the batch fell back to it) with its calibration points and samples. " else ""`Search a compound by
name; the arrow keys up / down go to the previous / next compound, left / right switch between the
modes. Click legend entries to hide or show groups; hover over a point for its details. On log axes,
the zero calibrant (Cal0) is drawn as a short line at the left edge.

```{r}
#| label: calcurve-viewer
# The viewer of the app (app/www/calcurve_viewer.js), with the data of the global curve and of each
# batch; the compounds removed before calibration with their calibration points only
samples_info <- as.data.frame(smp)
rownames(samples_info) <- samples_info$sample_id
if (!is.null(cal_avg) && nrow(cal_avg) > 0) {   # Averaged calibration points (option)
  ca <- as.data.frame(cal_avg)
  rownames(ca) <- ca$sample_id
  ca$.ctrl_cat <- "CalCurve"
  samples_info <- dplyr::bind_rows(samples_info, ca[, intersect(names(ca), names(samples_info))])
  rownames(samples_info) <- c(smp$sample_id, ca$sample_id)
}
removed_why <- stats::setNames(dplyr::coalesce(as.character(removed_tgt$reason), "no signal"), removed_tgt$feature_id)
removed_part <- function(batch = NULL) {
  if (nrow(removed_tgt) == 0) return(NULL)
  show$calib_view_removed(norm_all, MAT, removed_tgt$feature_id, removed_why, batch = batch)
}
cv_views <- list()
if (multi_batch) cv_views[["Global"]] <- list(parts = list(show$calib_view_of_global(gcal, samples_info), removed_part()))
for (b in batch_ids) {
  cv_views[[batch_label(b)]] <- list(parts = list(show$calib_view_of_batch(lst[[b]], BLK), removed_part(b)))
}
cv_data <- show$calib_viewer_data(
  compounds = data.frame(id = tcomps$feature_id, name = tcomps$feature_name),
  views = cv_views, log_scale = in_log, unit = unit,
  y_title = "Normalized, blank-subtracted signal", class_colors = class_colors
)
show$calib_viewer_html("calcurve-viewer", cv_data, script = file.path(app_root, "www", "calcurve_viewer.js"))
```

## 4.5 Concentration

The concentrations of each compound in all samples of all batches, per class: a box per class and
the samples as points. `r if (LLOX_IMPUTED) "Points of values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules are coloured as in the exported tables (red: not detected, LLOQ/4; yellow: detected but not quantified, LLOQ/2; blue: set to the LLOQ)." else paste0("Values below the LOD (n.d.) and the LLOQ (n.q.) have no value and are not shown (", sum(conc_long$conc_flag %in% 'n.d.' & is.na(conc_long$conc)), " n.d. and ", sum(conc_long$conc_flag %in% 'n.q.' & is.na(conc_long$conc)), " n.q. values of samples and QCs); blue points were set to the LLOQ.")`
Hover over a point for the sample; switch between linear and log axis.

```{r}
#| results: asis
# One entry per compound with concentrations; samples by index in the shared sample table
conc_q <- conc_long |> filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(kind = as.integer(show$imputed_kind(conc, lloq)) - 1L)
conc_data <- conc_q |> group_by(feature_name) |> group_split() |> lapply(function(d) {
  c(list(name = d$feature_name[1]), npts(s = unname(s_idx[d$sample_name]), y = sig(d$conc), k = d$kind))
})
class_cols <- vapply(sort(unique(conc_q$Class)), function(cl) {
  g <- smp$group[match(cl, smp$Class)]
  unname(if (g %in% names(group_colors)) group_colors[[g]] else "#999999")
}, character(1))
cat('<div class="viewer" id="concv">',
    '<div class="controls"><input type="search" class="search" placeholder="Search…" size="14"><button type="button" class="prev">&#9664;</button><select class="sel"></select>',
    '<button type="button" class="next">&#9654;</button>',
    '<label><input type="checkbox" class="log"> Log scale</label></div>',
    '<div class="plot" style="height:480px;"></div></div>',
    '<script>window.CONCVIEW = ',
    to_json(list(comps = conc_data, kinds = names(show$imputed_colors),
                 kind_colors = unname(show$imputed_colors), class_colors = as.list(class_cols),
                 unit = unit)),
    ';</script>', sep = "")
```

### 4.5.1 Average and median per compound

Statistics of the study samples only (no QCs), from the measured values at or above the LLOQ: values
`r if (LLOX_IMPUTED) "replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules" else "below the LOD / LLOQ (n.d. / n.q.) or set to the LLOQ"` are left out, as in the exported tables. *All batches* pools the measured
values of all batches; *n* is the number of these values. Concentrations in `r unit`.

```{r}
# Measured values (as `msdial$measured_conc()` of the exports): study samples, at or above the
# LLOQ, not replaced (unchanged from conc0)
meas <- conc_long |>
  filter(.ctrl_cat == "", !is.na(conc), conc >= lloq, conc == conc0) |>
  mutate(Batch = batch_label(as.character(batch_id)))
conc_stats <- function(d) summarise(d, n = n(), Average = round(mean(conc), 3),
                                    Median = round(stats::median(conc), 3),
                                    Min = round(min(conc), 3), Max = round(max(conc), 3), .groups = "drop")
stats_tbl <- bind_rows(
  meas |> group_by(Compound = feature_name) |> conc_stats() |> mutate(Batch = "All batches"),
  if (length(batch_ids) > 1) meas |> group_by(Compound = feature_name, Batch) |> conc_stats()
) |>
  select(Compound, Batch, n, Average, Median, Min, Max) |>
  arrange(Compound, Batch != "All batches", Batch) |>
  mutate(Batch = factor(Batch, levels = c("All batches", batch_label(batch_ids))))
if (nrow(stats_tbl) == 0) note("No measured concentrations at or above the LLOQ in the study samples.") else
  dt(stats_tbl, search = FALSE)
```



## 4.6 QC samples in acquisition order

One compound at a time: its concentration in each QC sample of all batches (each batch with its own
calibration) along the injection order, a line per QC group; the values should be stable over the run.
Filled points are measured values, open points values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules. Choose the compound
in the dropdown or search; hover over a point for the sample.

```{r}
#| results: asis
qc_long <- filter(conc_long, .ctrl_cat == "QC")
qc_comp <- qc_long |> group_by(feature_name) |> filter(any(!is.na(conc) | !is.na(conc_flag))) |> ungroup()
if (!has_qc) note(NO_QC) else if (nrow(qc_comp) == 0) note("No concentrations in the QC samples.") else {
  qc_classes <- sort(unique(as.character(qc_comp$Class)))
  qc_view <- list(
    kinds = names(show$imputed_colors), unit = unit,
    group_colors = as.list(show$hue_colors(qc_classes)),   # As in the app
    comps = qc_comp |> mutate(kind = as.integer(show$imputed_kind(conc, lloq)) - 1L) |>
      arrange(feature_name, injection_order) |> group_by(feature_name) |> group_split() |>
      # I(): arrays also for a single QC sample
      lapply(function(d) list(name = d$feature_name[1], s = I(unname(s_idx[d$sample_name])), y = I(sig(d$conc)),
                              k = I(d$kind), f = I(d$conc_flag)))
  )
  cat('<div class="viewer" id="qcv">',
      '<div class="controls"><input type="search" class="search" placeholder="Search…" size="14"><button type="button" class="prev">&#9664;</button><select class="sel"></select>',
      '<button type="button" class="next">&#9654;</button>',
      '<label><input type="checkbox" class="log"> Log scale</label></div>',
      '<div class="info"></div><div class="plot" style="height:460px;"></div></div>',
      '<script>window.QCVIEW = ', to_json(qc_view), ';</script>', sep = "")
}
```
